status: Five-post independent peer review complete; five findings accepted, applied by root, and verified resolved

scope.restriction: No article, shared-file, staging, commit, push, or reset actions performed by this reviewer.

method: Read the full visible text of all five finished HTML articles, including every authored gallery card and source note, and the complete corresponding audit JSONs. Independently checked consequential claims and quotations against selected primary passages through browsing and, where the browser parser failed, public source downloads or previously saved source files. Reviewed argument representation, specificity, length, repeated cautions, manufactured contrasts, universal religion claims, and references to abandoned copy. This is a selective source audit, not a claim to have reread all five complete books.
overall_conclusion: No material factual or quotation error found in the reviewed claims. One representation weakness understated the strength of Frankl's happiness claim before evaluating it. Four additional prose findings concerned an abandoned lineage claim, a duplicated survival caution, and two unnecessary cautions in Imperfection. Root applied all five refinements. James and Perennial Philosophy require no correction from this review. The varied examples and distinctions justify the remaining length; no broad compression or further rewrite is recommended.

priority_scale.P2: Worth fixing before publication: weak argument representation or a distracting remnant of abandoned framing.
priority_scale.P3: Targeted editorial improvement; no factual error.

findings.finding: The paragraph originally paraphrased the happiness argument as a modest observation about giving attention to a commitment, then denied that commitment reliably ends distress. The 1984 postscript actually makes the stronger claim that happiness follows automatically once a reason is found. The objection should address that claim and happiness rather than broad distress.
findings.primary_location: POSTSCRIPT 1984, The Case for a Tragic Optimism; PDF zero-based page 60 / human PDF page 61, extracted web lines 2531 to 2534. This PDF page number is not the printed pagination of every edition.
findings.exact_primary_sentence: Once the reason is found, however, one becomes happy automatically.
findings.proposed_change: State the automatic happiness claim explicitly, then say the case reports do not demonstrate that guarantee. Keep the concluding protection against blaming a person for continuing unhappiness.
findings.resolution: Root replaced the paragraph with a faithful paraphrase of the stronger postscript claim and a specific limit on its demonstrated support. Verified current HTML at line 287.

findings.finding: The CBT paragraph ended by denying descent from Fox, although the rewrite no longer claimed any historical lineage. The sentence argued against removed copy. The comparison of actual methods remained useful.
findings.original_sentence: An interest in thought proves neither descent from Fox nor the Golden Key's effectiveness.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the final sentence and retain the concrete comparison of CBT methods with Fox's mental causation claims.
findings.resolution: Root deleted that sentence. Independently verified the current CBT paragraph ends with the Beck Institute comparison.

findings.finding: The hero ended with a survival disclaimer that the developed opening and Christmas-deaths discussion already justified. It made the opening repeat its qualification before the reader encountered the evidence.
findings.original_sentence: His survival cannot prove why others died.
findings.proposed_change: Delete that sentence from the hero, keeping the specific reasons to keep living.
findings.resolution: Verified the current hero ends after the reasons Frankl describes; the substantive survival discussion remains in the body.

findings.finding: The bowl paragraph still denied that damage was beneficial and discussed whether the bowl became more valuable. The rewrite no longer asserted either proposition. These sentences retained the correction to old copy as published prose and distracted from the concrete repair.
findings.original_text: The visible break is evidence of work, not proof that the damage was beneficial. The photograph tells us nothing about whether the bowl became more valuable.
findings.proposed_change: Keep only the two concrete sentences about lacquer, gold, and someone fitting the pieces together.
findings.resolution: Root made that cut; verified the current bowl paragraph contains only those two concrete repair sentences.

findings.finding: The Nan-in card added a teacher-infallibility disclaimer that was not needed to interpret this story. Its preceding sentence already explained the visitor's obstacle. The source note separately and appropriately limits the historical status of the telling.
findings.original_sentence: Examining an assumption doesn't require treating the teacher as infallible.
findings.proposed_change: Delete that final interpretation sentence. Keep the first interpretation sentence and the literary-source note.
findings.resolution: Root deleted it; verified the current card keeps the first interpretation sentence.

posts.conclusion: No actionable correction found. The post reconstructs James's criteria and cases, preserves his interest in religious experience, and distinguishes experiencer authority from a public obligation to accept its theology. It does not incorrectly present him as either a simple debunker or an uncritical advocate.

posts.conclusion: No actionable correction found. The post gives perennialism an actual metaphysical argument, acknowledges Huxley's own identity/similarity qualification, and tests a concrete disputed Buddhist passage. Katz and Forman are presented as competing arguments with remaining questions, rather than a settled academic verdict.

Huxley's practice and epistemic argument in the 1945 book introduction

posts.length_and_voice: The explicit four-claim structure, textual comparison, and methodological dispute sustain the length. Some concise orienting cautions repeat later evidence, but none rose to a meaningful revision request. The ending names a concrete question about identifying the experiences.
posts.limits: The article and this review do not settle every historical Buddhist interpretation of buddha-nature. Modern translations are checked as identified translations. The primary texts support the portrayed positions without proving the underlying metaphysics.

posts.conclusion: No material folklore, quotation, or edition error found. The revised article accurately retains responsibility alongside imperfection and identifies the five-card selection as editorial rather than claiming all five items are in the book. HUM-04 and HUM-05 were applied and verified.
